chapters.title: 1. Trump calls the Iran war militarily effectively over as Massie files impeachment articles against Hegseth — Who holds the power to make war in a republic, and what is the remedy when that power is used without consent? Is accountability after victory still accountability?
2. Stephen Miller starts as White House chief of staff — After a defeat, does a leader owe the voters a change of course, or only a change of tactics? Is loyalty in an advisor a virtue or a danger?

3. Dave Chappelle jokes he feels better since Charlie Kirk was murdered; Erika Kirk calls it moral decay — Are there limits to laughter? Does free speech protect a joke from moral judgment, or only from punishment?

4. Pope Leo meets clergy-abuse survivors and urges religions to build bridges in Buenos Aires — Can an institution that caused deep harm still speak with moral authority? What is the difference between repentance and reform?
